title: Encryption-at-rest design and RBACv2 ownership matrix
body:
Purpose and scope:

This working doc captures the current proposed encryption-at-rest architecture coupled with RBACv2 ownership semantics, an actionable key rotation & escalation runbook, and the audit-to-SIEM evidence automation mapping. Intended audience: security engineers, infra, SRE, and compliance reviewers.

High level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Ensure all customer data at rest is encrypted with tenant-scoped KEKs where required (BYOK for regulated customers).
- Define clear role boundaries in RBACv2 for KMS operations (create/use/rotate/expire/revoke/backup-restore).
- Produce an audit log schema that supports automated evidence extraction for audits and SIEM ingestion.
- Create an operational runbook for rotation failures with escalation thresholds and automated evidence export.

Architecture overview (short):
- Envelope encryption for all storage tiers: object store (S3/GCS), RDS snapshots, blob caches, and metrics backups.
- KEK (Key Encryption Key) hierarchy: TenantKEK -> ServiceKEKs -> DataKeys. TenantKEKs can be Redwood-managed or BYOK (customer-provided HSM).
- HSM fallback: if BYOK HSM path is unavailable, use pre-authorized Redwood-managed escrow key with documented SLA and customer notification flow.

RBACv2 ownership matrix (summary):
Roles defined in RBACv2 and their KMS permissions (permission categories simplified):
- security-admin: full KMS management (create_key, delete_key, rotate_key, set_policy, export_audit). Not usable by product teams.
- platform-ops: service-level key operations (create_service_key, rotate_service_key, schedule_rotation). Cannot access Tenant BYOK material.
- tenant-admin: for BYOK onboarding and key binding operations (initiate_binding, request_hsm_provision). Limited to tenant scope only.
- srep (SRE/Incident responder): emergency-use decrypt-only tokens for specific recovery actions (time-limited), cannot rotate keys.
- auditor: read-only access to audit exports and evidence bundles, no key usage permissions.

Ownership matrix (example rows):
- Key scope: TenantKEK (BYOK) -> Owner: tenant-admin + security-admin for policy overrides.
- Key scope: TenantKEK (Redwood-managed) -> Owner: security-admin + platform-ops for lifecycle.
- Key scope: ServiceKEK -> Owner: platform-ops.
- Key scope: DataKey (per-dataset) -> Owner: platform-ops with automatic rotation.

Mapping to RBACv2 policies (short examples):
- Policy: allow(resourceType="kms/keys", action=["rotate"], resourceScope="service/*") -> Role: platform-ops
- Policy: deny(resourceType="kms/material", action=["export","backup"], resourceScope="tenant/byok/*") -> Role: platform-ops

Audit log schema (core fields - flat JSON event representation for SIEM ingestion):
- event_id: stable unique id (uuid)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- actor_id: internal user id (svc- or user-)
- actor_role: RBACv2 role at time of action (security-admin, platform-ops, tenant-admin, etc.)
- action: canonical action name (kms.create_key, kms.rotate_key, kms.decrypt, kms.bind_byok, kms.hsm_fallback)
- resource_type: kms/key | kms/key_version | storage/object | db/snapshot
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier (projects/..../keys/..../versions/..)
- key_id: key uuid (if applicable)
- key_version: semver-like version or key version id
- rotation_started_at: ISO8601 (if rotation action)
- rotation_completed_at: ISO8601 (nullable)
- status: success | failure | in_progress
- outcome: short text with machine-friendly codes (e.g., OK, TIMEOUT, SIGNATURE_VERIFY_FAIL)
- correlation_id: request correlation id / trace id
- request_latency_ms: integer
- client_ip: egress IP (masked per privacy rules)
- audit_evidence_refs: list of artifact URIs (GCS path, SIEM doc id)

Note: audit_evidence_refs is a string field containing a comma-separated list of URIs to keep the schema flat for downstream exporters. See evidence automation section.

Event example (single-line JSON for ingestion):
{"event_id":"d4f9c8b2-3a2e-4b2a-9f3b-7d4b1f2c9a9f","timestamp":"2025-02-14T18:22:03Z","actor_id":"svc-keymgr","actor_role":"platform-ops","action":"kms.rotate_key","resource_type":"kms/key","resource_id":"projects/prod/keys/tenant-1234","key_id":"k-9f3b7d4b","key_version":"v3","rotation_started_at":"2025-02-14T18:20:00Z","rotation_completed_at":"2025-02-14T18:22:00Z","status":"success","outcome":"OK","correlation_id":"trace-8a7c","request_latency_ms":"120","client_ip":"10.2.3.4","audit_evidence_refs":"gs://redwood-audit/tenant-1234/rotation/2025-02-14/evidence.tar.gz"} 

SIEM export mapping (elastic-style field mapping suggestions):
- ecs.event.id -> event_id
- '@timestamp' -> timestamp
- user.id -> actor_id
- user.role -> actor_role
- event.action -> action
- service.type -> resource_type
- service.id -> resource_id
- outcome -> outcome
- url.original -> audit_evidence_refs (or file.path)

Export mechanics (evidence automation pipeline):
1) KMS action emits structured audit event to internal audit-bus (Kafka topic: audit.kms.v2).
2) Audit-bus triggers a formatter lambda that normalizes fields and attaches artifact references.
3) Formatter writes a compressed evidence bundle to GCS with predictable path: gs://redwood-audit/{tenant}/{action}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{correlation_id}/evidence.tar.gz
4) Formatter pushes an enriched event to SIEM-export topic with audit_evidence_refs set to the GCS path.
5) SIEM connector pulls enriched events and ingests into Elastic (ECS mapping).
6) Long-term evidence retention: evidence bundles are copied to cold-storage bucket with retention metadata and recorded in compliance ledger (immutable).

Evidence bundle contents (expected):
- signed-kms-call-trace.log (raw request/response headers redacted)
- ksv-verify.txt (HSM signature verification output if applicable)
- rotation-checksum-manifest.json (checksums of rotated key material backups)
- runbook-execution.log (if runbook triggered automatically or manually)
- incident-ticket-ref.txt (JIRA id)

Rotation runbook (practical):
Pre-reqs: successful pre-rotation test must pass (kdf verification, crypto self-check) and monitoring targets at green.

Automated rotation flow:
- Step 1: schedule_rotation(job_id) -> system starts rotation and emits rotation_started event.
- Step 2: create new key version; rewrap DEKs; run smoke decrypts; verify signatures; emit per-object rewrap events.
- Step 3: if all smoke decrypts OK -> mark rotation_completed and schedule old-version retirement after TTL.

Failure handling (automated thresholds):
- If >0.5% object rewrap failures across a customer corpus within 10m -> auto-pause rotation and create incident (JIRA-SEC-ROT-{job_id}).
- If rotation process exceeds 30m for >90% of objects -> trigger platform-ops escalation.
- If HSM signing fails in >3 attempts -> switch to HSM fallback policy (see HSM fallback below) and notify tenant-admin and security-admin.

Escalation matrix (contacts are role placeholders):
- T+0-10m: platform-ops on-call notified (pager).
- T+10-30m: on-call lead + security-admin paged.
- T+30-60m: incident declared, SRE war room, compliance notified if tenant is regulated.

HSM fallback policy (short):
- Condition: BYOK HSM unresponsive or signature verification fails consistently for binding calls.
- Action: failover to Redwood-managed escrow key only with pre-authorized escrow entries (customer policy must have pre-approved fallback at onboarding).
- Evidence: generate fallback_decision.json inside evidence bundle with the following fields: reason, invoked_by, timestamp, fallback_key_id, authorization_refs.
- Notification: automated email + secure channel to tenant-admin and security-admin, include correlation_id.

Operational checklists (for runbook responders):
- Verify audit-bus event stream is receiving kms.rotate_key events.
- Pull evidence bundle: gsutil cp gs://.../evidence.tar.gz /tmp/; verify checksums.
- Validate key versions and ensure read paths unaffected by serving runtime.
- Escalate per matrix and attach evidence bundle to incident ticket.

Open questions & follow-ups (todo):
- Decide canonical retention period for evidence bundles for non-regulated vs regulated tenants (suggestion: 90d / 7y).
- Determine whether audit_evidence_refs should be a separate document store record instead of comma-separated string for easier queries.
- Confirm exact SIEM field mapping with SOC (elastic field names vs. Splunk conventions).
- Add test harness for simulating HSM failures and validating fallback paths end-to-end.

Appendix: quick grep-ready queries for SIEM (example)
- Find failed rotations in last 24h: event.action: "kms.rotate_key" AND status: "failure" | sort by @timestamp desc
- Rotation failures by tenant: group_by resource_id, count where outcome != "OK"

Notes (style): this is a working draft. Some sections intentionally terse. Expect follow-ups from platform-ops and SOC about mapping names and retention TTLs.

-- Arjun
